evidence.clarity: H1 'What close needs to tell open.' is insider shorthand a stranger has to decode, but the lead directly under it ('a shared logbook for restaurant managers. What ran out, who called in sick, what needs fixing') settles what and who, and the CTA 'Start a free trial' carries 'Takes you to app.shiftnote.example to sign up.' At 1440, 768 and 390 all of it sits above the fold.
evidence.fit: Removes every template logo and testimonial, keeps logo.svg and both colours (indigo buttons, coral #FF7A59 tags and margin rule), and all three CTAs point to https://app.shiftnote.example/signup. The phone-reading manager is served well. The paying owner gets one step card ('Sunday night: The owner reads the whole week') and nothing that shows what the owner would actually see.
evidence.distinctiveness: The hero artifact is a ruled notebook page with a coral margin rule, timestamps in the margin and serif 'handwriting' entries (8:15 pm 'Ran out', 10:40 pm 'Called in'). With the logo removed you would still read it as a restaurant logbook. The rest of the page follows a familiar arc: three-step row, category list, 'Why not the group chat?' and a full-bleed indigo CTA band.
evidence.proof: At 1440 a complete example handover (four tagged entries, 'Written by Dani, 11:48 pm') is in the first viewport, and its times match the 11:48 pm step below. It is a static picture, though: nothing shows an item being picked up or owned. The 'What goes in the log' section restages the same four tags on a second ruled sheet and adds no new evidence.
evidence.craft: The type scale is tight (heavy sans H1, serif log entries), the palette is restrained, axe reports 0 violations and nothing overflows at any width. Defects: at 1440 the left column is empty from y≈610 to the fold beside the tall log; the second ruled sheet in 'What goes in the log' repeats the hero; at 390/768 the log entries load at near-zero opacity (staggered fade), so a quick screenshot shows a blank ruled page.
evidence.mobile: 390: H1, lead, full-width-ish CTA (52px) and the 'Read an example handover' link fit in the first screen, and the log header starts at y≈551. No overflow at 390 or 320. There is no mobile menu: the nav links are simply dropped, leaving logo plus a 40px header CTA. The 'Read an example handover' link is a 26px-tall target. The layout is a straight stack rather than a recomposition.
evidence.honesty: 'Example handover' kicker sits at the top of the artifact at every width. The CTA note says where the button goes before you click. The closing band 'No logos to show you. No case studies yet.' is candid without grovelling, though it is a whole section about what the company lacks. Nothing is invented.
evidence.interaction: There are no controls beyond links. I clicked each one: the three 'Start a free trial' links go to the brief's signup URL, the nav anchors #how and #log resolve, and at 390/768 'Read an example handover' jumps to #example (the link is hidden at 1440). The artifact is honestly static, so the visitor has nothing to try. No console errors.
evidence.copy: Specific, restaurant-native language: '86'd the halibut', 'there's a wedge under it for now', 'The binder stays at the host stand, where the closer isn't and the owner never is', 'That's the whole product.' Terms stay consistent and there is no buzzword. The only weakness is that the H1 relies on the reader already thinking in 'close/open'.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: a specific promise, an example log beside it and an honest CTA with its destination, all in one viewport. 390: promise and CTA are in view, but only the artifact's header ('Tuesday close for Wednesday open') shows above the fold, and the entries are still fading in. The promise ('what close needs to tell open') is evocative rather than an outcome.

problems: The core artifact is static: nothing shows an item being owned or followed up, so the product reads as 'a notes page' and the visitor has nothing to try.
The paying owner gets one step card and no view of their own (no week view or summary), so the brief's second audience is underserved.
Rhythm: dead area beside the hero log at 1440, and 'What goes in the log' repeats the hero artifact instead of adding information; the mobile layout is stacked rather than recomposed and has no menu.

evidence.clarity: H1 'Nothing from tonight's close gets lost by tomorrow's open.' plus a lead naming the product (shift logbook), the audience (restaurant managers), the job (ran out / called in / needs fixing) and the mechanism ('every item keeps an owner until it's handled'). The CTA is followed by 'Opens the signup page at app.shiftnote.example. No sales call; you set it up yourself.'
evidence.fit: Builds a separate path for each reader: STEP 1 closer composer, STEP 2 opener's 'Sam opened the note' view, STEP 3 owner's 'Week of 13 Oct' table, captioned 'The owner usually reads this one on a laptop; on a phone it stacks.' Template proof is gone, logo.svg and both colours are kept (indigo CTAs and handled state, coral #FF7A59 open-state dots), and every primary CTA goes to the brief's signup URL. Coral survives only as small status dots, which is a thin use of a brand colour.
evidence.distinctiveness: A ticket/close-sheet language runs through the page: monospace timestamps, outlined uppercase tags (86, REPAIR, CASH), dashed rules under each sheet header and a serif display face. The structure follows the note's life from close to open to owner, so it comes from the product. It is less evocative than a physical-notebook metaphor, and in places the bordered boxes read as generic UI.
evidence.proof: At 1440 the close note with working 'Mark handled' buttons is in the first viewport. Clicking it on 'Walk-in reading 41°F' switched the dot from coral to indigo, changed the text to 'Handled · Sam, <time>' and turned the button into 'Undo'. The week table's '5 closes · 2 still open' matches its two open rows. This answers the real doubt: does anything make sure the item gets picked up?
evidence.craft: Clear hierarchy (large serif H1, grey lead, mono meta), consistent 1px ink borders and spacing, axe 0 violations, smallest text 13px. Defects: at 768 the note is a ~510px column pinned left, leaving ~230px dead on the right; chips and 'Mark handled' are 40px tall; at 390 the 'Guest' chip wraps alone onto a second row; some H2s run long ('One note, written once, read by three people who need different things from it.').
evidence.mobile: 390: H1, lead and a full-width 48px CTA with its destination note are in the first screen, and the 'Close note' sheet starts at y≈572. The Menu button opened a clean panel (aria-expanded=true, label became 'Close'), and Escape closed it. The owner table recomposes into stacked rows ('Owner: Sam · Handled Wed 10:40 am'), and tapping 'Mark handled' shows its state change on the tapped row. No overflow at 390/320 on load. Under 44px: chips and Mark handled (40px).
evidence.honesty: The figcaption reads 'Sample note… The restaurant and the people are made up; nothing you press here is saved or sent', the composer hint says 'Sample only; nothing is sent', and the week view is captioned 'Sample week'. At 390 the figcaption sits at the bottom of the note (y≈1549), so the first screen shows the sample without its label. The 'no customer names or quotes' statement appears both in the hero and in the footer, which repeats the point.
evidence.interaction: All three widths: 'Mark handled' → handled state plus an aria-live message, and 'Undo' restores 'Open · Sam, opening Wed'. Composer: picked 'Repair', clicked 'Add to tonight's note', and the entry landed under 'Tonight's note so far', the empty text hid and the input refilled with a new suggestion; Enter also adds. Weaknesses: submitting empty gives only a screen-reader message (visually just a focus ring); an unbroken pasted string (a URL plus 80 characters) pushed the page 577px wider than the 390 viewport; the 'Handled · Sam' time uses the real clock (it showed 1:00 pm), which breaks the Wednesday-morning story.
evidence.copy: Grounded and specific: 'Deposit bag is in the safe, not dropped', 'The ones nobody picked up are the ones that show', 'What stays out: Schedules, the POS, inventory counts and payroll'. Button labels say what they do ('Add to tonight's note', 'Mark handled'). Some sentences are long, and the hero lead runs about 40 words. Small slip: STEP 2 is timed 9:38 AM even though the note says someone had to be in by 9:30.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: a specific outcome for a named audience, an operable sample note that makes it believable, a CTA with its destination, and a line explaining the sample, all in one viewport. 390: promise, full-width CTA with destination and the top of the note are in view, but the sample label and the first 'Mark handled' control sit below the fold.

problems: An unbroken pasted string in the composer (for example a long URL) makes the whole page scroll sideways at 390 (577px extra), and an empty submit gives no visible feedback.
The sample label sits at the bottom of the hero note, below the fold at 390, and the handled timestamp uses the visitor's real clock, which breaks the sample's Wednesday-morning story.
Coral is reduced to tiny status dots, several targets are 40px, and the 768 layout leaves a dead strip beside a left-pinned note column.

reason: B turns the product's actual promise (every item keeps an owner until handled) into something you can operate in the first screen, and gives the paying owner a real week view that recomposes on the phone. A has the more evocative visual idea (the ruled notebook) and tighter copy, but its artifact is a static picture and the owner gets one line. I would change my mind if B's interactive pieces felt like added volume rather than proof, or if the notebook motif tested much better with restaurant managers.
